title: Vegan Strawberry Milk Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vegan cupcakes with real strawberry puree, ready in about 45 minutes with 20 minutes hands-on prep.
description: These cupcakes taste like a glass of strawberry milk in cake form. I use real strawberry puree in the batter and the frosting, so the pink color comes from the fruit, not a bottle. The crumb stays soft and moist thanks to plant milk and oil, no eggs or dairy needed. It tastes light, fruity, and just sweet enough. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen three times to get the puree ratio right. Too much liquid makes a gummy cupcake, so I reduce the puree first to concentrate the flavor. Frost these with the strawberry buttercream once they cool completely. A few freeze dried strawberry pieces on top make a nice natural garnish.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups fresh strawberries, hulled and chopped
1/2 cup unsweetened plant milk (oat or soy)
1/3 cup neutral oil, such as canola or sunflower
1 tbsp freeze dried strawberries, crushed, for garnish
instructions: Puree 1 1/2 cups strawberries in a blender until smooth.
Simmer the puree in a small pot for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it reduces to about 1/2 cup. Let it cool fully.
Preheat your oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 liners.
Whisk flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, mix plant milk, oil, vanilla, vinegar, and 1/4 cup of the cooled strawberry puree.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir just until combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, beat vegan butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar and the remaining strawberry puree.
Beat the frosting on medium speed for 2 minutes until light and fluffy, then pipe onto the cooled cupcakes.
Top each cupcake with a pinch of crushed freeze dried strawberries.
tips: Reduce the puree before adding it to the batter. This keeps the cupcakes from turning dense or wet.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe well.
Use room temperature vegan butter so the frosting whips up smooth with no lumps.
Freeze dried strawberries add color and crunch without extra liquid, so they work better than fresh slices on top.

faq.question: Why is my strawberry cupcake batter pink instead of the frosting?
faq.answer: That happens when the puree is too watery and spreads color through the whole batter fast. Reducing the puree on the stove first fixes this and keeps the color soft and even.

faq.question: Can I use frozen strawberries instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw them fully and drain extra liquid before blending. Frozen berries can add more water, so you may need a minute or two longer to reduce the puree.

faq.question: Why do I need to reduce the strawberry puree first?
faq.answer: Raw puree has too much water for this batter and can make the crumb gummy. Cooking it down concentrates the flavor and keeps the texture light.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes gluten free?
faq.answer: Swap the all-purpose flour for a 1:1 gluten free baking blend. The texture stays soft, though the crumb may be slightly more delicate.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove you do not need dye to get a pretty pink treat. The real strawberry flavor comes through in every bite, from the soft cake to the fluffy frosting.
